newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France says strike wave losing it passengers.
newsitem.headline: Air France says strike wave losing it passengers.

text.p: Air France said on Monday it had lost 121,500 passengers since the start of a wave of strikes 10 days ago to protest against the state-owned carrier's restructuring plans.

In a statement, it accused unions and the media of misleading the public over the impact of the wildcat walkouts by employees at its regional airline Air France Europe who are unhappy over merger terms with its parent Air France.
The merger is part of Air France's plans to get ready for privatisation, expected later this year or in 1998.
"We have lost 121,500 passengers since the start of the conflict on March 27," an airline spokeswoman said.
Air France said the public had been encouraged by some unions and the media to believe the situation at Paris Orly airport was worse than it actually was.

Last Friday alone, when all flights were operating, Air France lost 12,500 passengers because of exaggerated threats of disruption the day before, she said. The actual disruption turned to be minor, she said.

"This total overexposure in the media is considerably damaging Air France's domestic activity. Its reservations have fallen sharply even though the schedule is being maintained 100 percent and conditions are perfectly normal," it said.

Air France did not say how many reservations it had lost since the employees of Air France Europe began the disruptions over the merger terms. The Air France Europe employees have traditionally received better pay and benefits than their colleagues at Air France.
But the spokeswoman said the "no show" rate -- the proportion of passengers with bookings who fail to check in -- had doubled to 24 or 26 percent in the past week from the usual 12 percent.
Cargo operations were barely affected, however, she said.
A Paris court ruled on Saturday that Air France Europe unions could no longer stage wildcat strikes and had to give management at least five days' notice.
